title: Uniform scalar transition between primitive-root source charts
statement: Fix the finite purity setting P [def-pur-conventions], with algebraically closed base field k, coefficient prime ell distinct from its characteristic, coefficient ring A=O_E/(varpi_E^n), n>=1, and N=ell^n. Let d be a nonnegative integer and let zeta and eta be primitive N-th roots in k. Use the specified source charts t_zeta(f,K): Lf^*K(d)[2d] ≅ (Lf^*K)[2d] of [def-pur-finite-reduction-root-charts], on the intrinsic small pro-etale derived categories. There is one natural number r, independent of schemes, morphisms and complexes, such that for every k-scheme X, every scheme Y, every morphism f:X→Y and every intrinsic complex K on Y, t_zeta(f,K)^{-1} followed by t_eta(f,K) is r times the identity of (Lf^*K)[2d]. Scalar multiplication here is repeated addition of a morphism. No finiteness or separatedness of X,Y,f and no boundedness of K are required.

source.place: Middle identification in the displayed composite, expanded using the root charts of def-pur-finite-reduction-root-charts; agent calculation of the change of root.

proof.text: Put N = ell^n. The two primitive roots generate the same cyclic roots group. Write eta=zeta^a with a prime to N, and choose c with ac=1 modulo N. On constant scalar generators, the root-line trivialization at eta is a times the one at zeta, by the section formula of def-pur-finite-reduction-root-charts and the primitive-root basis lem-pur-primitive-root-etale-basis. Since N annihilates the coefficient ring, their inverses differ by c.

Apply the actual ordered tensor recursion of def-pur-finite-reduction-chart-calculus to these inverse shifted degree-one charts. Its zero term is unchanged and its successor is bilinear, so induction gives scalar c^d. The reassociation and unit factors do not involve roots. Exact comparison pullback, shift, tensoring with the arbitrary pulled-back complex, and coefficient realization are additive and preserve this natural-number multiple. Thus every source chart at eta is c^d times its chart at zeta. Composing with the inverse zeta chart proves the assertion with r=c^d, simultaneously in the scheme, morphism and complex. At d=0 this is 1; empty schemes and zero objects obey the same identity.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finiteReductionSourceChartScalar (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    (d : ℕ) (ζ η : P.field.k)
    (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ P.diagonalExponent)
    (hη : IsPrimitiveRoot η P.diagonalExponent) :
    ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))]
      (f : X ⟶ Y) (K : Scheme.proEtaleDerivedCategory Y P.Ring),
      (P.finiteReductionSourceTrivialization f d ζ hζ K).inv ≫
        (P.finiteReductionSourceTrivialization f d η hη K).hom =
          r • 𝟙 (((P.finiteReductionPullback f).obj K)⟦2 * (d : ℤ)⟧)
